message:
fix(host,viewer): epoch gate -- the first AU after a capture flush is the new epoch's IDR; a held resume frame is not the viewer's anchor

P11 (field 2026-09-07 15:15). The wire capture stamp is the front of the encoder's accepted-
input FIFO, and this hardware MFT (surface input path) returns the previous input's AU
during the current call. A flush empties the capture ring but not the encoder, so the first
call after the DXGI restore emitted the pre-switch picture: real, on the new generation,
820 ms behind its send time (seq 24484). The viewer took it as the resume anchor and read
the fresh frames behind it as an 848 ms decode backlog (Congested, IDR, burst drops).

Host:
- H264AccessUnit.inputEpoch rides the FIFO with the stamp and the synthetic flag;
  CaptureState::inputEpoch is bumped by ResetTimelineAnchors (every flush / restart /
  geometry confirm / encoder reset).
- host_epoch_gate.hpp: after a flush, an AU from an older epoch is discarded (key or not;
  it never satisfies the forced-key latch or the sender barrier), a current-epoch P before
  the IDR is discarded and the key re-forced, the first current-epoch keyframe opens the
  gate; past 700 ms / 12 AUs the encoder is rebuilt (the stale-output reset path). Nothing
  is held for later, so the old-stamp-then-fresh-burst shape cannot recur. Discards consume
  no seq. Logged, plus auEpoch/curEpoch/holdUs on the first-frame and feedback lines.
- The secure-desktop kick block is unchanged (that design is a separate scope).

Viewer (narrow): FrameGateInputs.sendQpcUs. In Normal, the frame that ends a >250 ms
silence anchors the decode-queue floor only if the host held it <= 300 ms (send - capture,
both host clock); a held one is shown but leaves the anchor pending for the first fresh
frame, bounded to 8 frames / 500 ms after which the old rule resumes (a genuine backlog
holds every frame and still trips).

Tests: remote60_host_encode_epoch_test on the real MFT via the product's D3D11 NV12
surface path reproduces the pre-flush AU 800 ms behind the first post-flush capture and
shows the gate sending the IDR first; gate rules and bounds on fabricated AUs; frame gate
+2 (held resume frame does not anchor; genuine backlog still trips); recovery S13 (both
pre-fix shapes: no congestion, no request) and S14 (fake host runs the product gate: the
first AU on the wire after Flush() is a key, viewer clean) -- 14/14. Field verification
pending (two UAC prompts; RDP must be off).
